recentItems.description:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has urged the Centre to provide immediate financial assistance to the state following extensive damage caused by two consecutive cyclones, Arnab and Murasu. During his meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Delhi, the Chief Minister stated that preliminary assessments indicate losses of more than ₹7,000 crore. He highlighted damage to standing crops, coastal infrastructure and the power supply system, and requested the Centre to release assistance as early as possible following the assessment by central teams. Chandrababu also presented proposals related to Andhra Pradesh's development, seeking funds for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub and additional support for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region. He explained the development plans for Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati, and discussed investment opportunities emerging from the recent Visakhapatnam Partnership Summit. State Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior finance department officials also attended the meeting.

recentItems.description:
Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan has directed Panchayat Raj, Rural Development and Rural Water Supply (RWS) officials to remain fully prepared to tackle the impact of Cyclone Aquan. During a review meeting with officials at his camp office, he stressed the need for advance relief measures in coastal villages and heightened vigilance in cyclone-affected districts, particularly on November 19 and 20. Districts under red alert must remain on high alert, and people living in coastal and low-lying areas should be shifted immediately to safer locations. Pawan Kalyan also directed officials to restore nearly 520 kilometres of rural roads reportedly damaged by recent cyclones. Expressing concern over the cyclone threat during the paddy harvest season, he called for measures to minimise crop losses and protect farmers. He instructed the entire administration, including field-level staff, to remain in villages until the cyclone threat completely subsides, with the protection of human lives as the top priority.

recentItems.description:
Cyclone Aquan has intensified over the southwest-central Bay of Bengal, raising concerns along the Andhra Pradesh coastline. Moving at a speed of around 3 kmph, the storm is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal tonight. According to the weather forecast mentioned in this report, it may further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning.

The cyclone is likely to make landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam on Friday afternoon. During landfall, wind speeds could reach 120–130 kmph, potentially causing rough sea conditions and posing a serious threat to coastal areas.

The evolving weather situation has put Andhra Pradesh's coastal districts on alert. Residents in vulnerable areas are advised to follow official weather bulletins and instructions issued by the authorities.

Watch this report for the latest cyclone updates, expected landfall location, wind speeds and the potential impact on Andhra Pradesh.
